title: Protease subsite profiling with proteome-derived peptide libraries \(PICS)
protocol: Culture cells in appropriate cell culture flasks.
Harvest cells when they reach 50% confluency.
Wash cells three times with PBS.
Grow cells in serum-free medium for 12-24 hours.
Collect harvested material from at least six culture flasks.
Decant medium from cell culture flasks.
Add protease inhibitors: 1.0 mM phenylmethylsulphonyl fluoride (PMSF), 10 μM trans-epoxysuccinyl-L-leucylamido(4-guanidino)butan (E-64), and 10 mM ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
Centrifuge at 2,200 g at 4 °C for 30 min; keep supernatant and discard pellet.
Add trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to a final concentration of 10% (vol/vol), incubate on ice for 1 h.
Centrifuge at 8,500 g at 4 °C for 1 h; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet twice with -20 °C methanol.
Air-dry for 10 min.
Overlay with 1 mL of 100 mM HEPES, 0.1% (wt/vol) SDS, pH 7.4.
Resuspend TCA pellet by mild ultrasonication for 30 min in a chilled bath.
Incubate the resuspended sample at -20°C (-80°C if necessary) for 1 hour.
Incubate the sample at 70°C for 30 minutes.
Quantify protein using bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assay or absorbance at 280 nm.
Dilute the solution 5-fold with 200 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, to a final SDS concentration of 0.02%.
Add 5 mM dithiothreitol (DTT).
Take 20 μl aliquot for SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) analysis.
Digest protein with trypsin at an enzyme/proteome ratio of 1:50, or use GluC or chymotrypsin.
Add 5 μg/ml DNase I and RNase E.
Incubate the sample at 37°C for 16 hours.
Add 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF).
Centrifuge the mixture at 40,000 x g for 0.5 hour.
Keep supernatant and discard pellet.
Take another 20 μl aliquot to control digest efficiency by SDS-PAGE analysis.
Wash cells three times with PBS.
Detach cells in PBS supplemented with 0.2% (wt/vol) EDTA.
Centrifuge cells at 400 g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Resuspend cells in 10 ml hypotonic lysis buffer containing protease inhibitors: 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 1.0 mM PMSF, 10 μM E-64, and 10 mM EDTA.
Lysate cells using nitrogen cavitation or repeated aspiration with needles.
Centrifuge cell lysate at 40,000 x g for 1 hour.
Precipitate the cell lysate with TCA to a final concentration of 10% (vol/vol).
Incubate on ice for 1 hour and centrifuge at 8,500 g at 4°C for 1 hour.
Discard supernatant.
Wash pellet twice with -20°C methanol.
Air-dry for 10 minutes.
Overlay with 1 mL of 100 mM HEPES pH 7.4, containing 0.1% (wt/vol) SDS.
Quantify protein using BCA assay and/or absorbance at 280 nm.
Dilute the solution 5-fold with 200 mM HEPES pH 7.4 to achieve a final SDS concentration of 0.02%, then add 5 mM DTT.
Take a 20 μL aliquot for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Perform specific endoproteolytic digestion using trypsin, GluC, or chymotrypsin at an enzyme/proteome ratio of 1:50.
Add 5 μg/ml DNase I and 5 μg/ml RNase E to the solution.
Incubate at 37°C for 16 hours.
Add 1 mM PMSF, then centrifuge at 40,000 x g for 0.5 hours.
Keep the supernatant; discard the pellet.
Take a 20 μL aliquot to control digest efficiency by SDS-PAGE.
Continue with sulfhydryl and amine protection steps.
Carefully remove remaining supernatant from the lysis pellet.
Resuspend the lysis pellet in 5 mL of 100 mM HEPES pH 7.4, containing 0.02% (wt/vol) SDS.
(Optional) Perform a freeze-thaw cycle on the lysis pellet to enhance lysis extent.
Incubate at 70°C for 30 minutes; then let cool to ambient temperature (~22°C).
Take a 100 μL aliquot, centrifuge at 14,000 g for 10 minutes, and determine the protein concentration of the supernatant using BCA assay.
Add 5 mM DTT.
Add 5 μg/ml DNase I and 5 μg/ml RNase E.
Incubate at 37°C for 2–3 h.
Keep a 20 μl aliquot for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Perform specific endoproteolytic digestion using trypsin, GluC, or chymotrypsin with an enzyme/proteome ratio of 1:50.
Incubate at 37°C for 16 h.
Add 1 mM PMSF and centrifuge at 40,000 x g for 0.5 h.
Keep the supernatant and discard the pellet.
Take a 20 μl aliquot to control digest efficiency by SDS-PAGE.
Add 5 mM DTT and incubate at 70°C for 30 min.
Let cool to 22°C.
Add 40 mM iodoacetamide.
Incubate at 22°C for 5 min.
Check that the pH remains between 7.0–7.5; adjust if necessary.
Incubate at 22°C for 3 h.
Add 10 mM DTT to quench remaining iodoacetamide.
Incubate at 22°C for 15 min.
Check that the pH remains between 7.0–7.5; adjust if necessary.
Add 10 mM formaldehyde and 10 mM NaCNBH₃, incubate for 3–16 h at 22°C.
Repeat the formaldehyde labeling once.
Buffer exchange samples to 10 mM potassium phosphate buffer, pH 2.7, and 20% (vol/vol) acetonitrile.
Load samples onto two self-packed XK 26/20 columns in tandem for preparative size exclusion chromatography using Sephadex G-10 resin.
Monitor peptide elution by absorption at 214 nm or 220 nm.
Collect PICS peptides for further purification based on the exclusion limit of 700 Da.
Perform strong cation exchange chromatography using sulfopropyl sepharose fast flow resin in self-packed columns.
Bind and wash samples in 10 mM potassium phosphate buffer, pH 2.7, and 20% (vol/vol) acetonitrile.
Monitor peptide binding and elution by absorption at 214 nm or 220 nm.
Perform extensive washing of the column (approximately 10 column volumes).
Elute peptides using a one-step gradient of 1 M NaCl in 10 mM potassium phosphate buffer, pH 2.7.
Remove acetonitrile by vacuum-evaporation.
Reduce sample volume by 50% and replenish with water.
Add 0.6% (vol/vol) formic acid to the sample for binding.
Wash with 0.3% (vol/vol) formic acid.
Elute with 80% (vol/vol) acetonitrile.
Concentrate eluate in a vacuum concentration system.
Resuspend in 0.5 ml water.
Take a 10 μl aliquot for peptide quantization by BCA assay.
Adjust concentration to 2-10 mg/ml.
Store at -70°C.
Thaw peptide library; use 200 μg library per protease if no clean-up is required before biotinylation, or 400 μg per protease if clean-up is required before biotinylation.
Adjust appropriate buffer conditions for the test protease (pH, type of buffer, reducing agents, co-factors).
Adjust peptide library concentration to 1 mg/ml.
Add activated protease at a ratio of 1:100 (wt/wt).
Incubate for 2 hours at a temperature suitable for the protease under investigation.
Heat deactivate the protease if necessary.
Acidify the sample with 0.1-0.5% trifluoracetic acid if primary amines or reducing substances are present.
Bind the acidified sample to C18 SPE cartridges.
Wash the column with 5 column volumes of 0.5% formic acid.
Elute the sample with 2 column volumes of 80% acetonitrile.
Vacuum-evaporate the eluted sample to near-dryness and reconstitute in 200 μl of 200 mM HEPES pH 7.4.
Control that the pH is between 7-8, adjust if necessary.
Prepare a 10 mM sulfo-NHS-SS-Biotin solution in DMSO immediately prior to use.
Incubate the PICS assay with sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin at 22°C for 2 hours.
Equilibrate high-capacity streptavidin Sepharose in 50 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.4.
Use a resin slurry volume of 1.5 times the volume of the PICS assay.
Add buffer-equilibrated streptavidin Sepharose to biotinylated PICS assay.
Incubate at 22°C for 0.5 hours with mild agitation.
Pour the incubated slurry into a spin column of sufficient volume with a filter of approximately 10 μm pore size.
Place the column in a 2 ml reaction tube.
Centrifuge column at 150 g for 1 min.
Adjust centrifugation speed as necessary to pass PICS assay solution through the column without drying it out.
Re-apply the first flow-through to resin and centrifuge a second time.
Discard flow-through after second centrifugation.
Wash resin with 500 μl of washing buffer.
Centrifuge column and discard flow-through.
Repeat washing eight times.
Prepare fresh elution buffer: 50 mM HEPES, 10 mM DTT, pH 7.4.
Press bottom plug in column.
Apply 500 μl of elution buffer to the top of the column.
Close column top with screw cap.
Incubate column for 2 hours at 22 °C with mild agitation.
Place column in a clean 2 ml reaction tube.
Remove bottom plug and loosen screw cap.
Centrifuge and keep eluate from first elution.
Place column in a second clean 2 ml reaction tube.
Apply 500 μl of elution buffer to the top of the column for a second elution.
Centrifuge and keep eluate from second elution.
Pool the two elution fractions.
Reconstitute the library amount with 1-5% of the estimated eluate amount (2-10 μg for a 200 μg library).
Acidify the sample with 0.5% (vol/vol) formic acid.
Bind the sample to a reversed-phase SPE C18 cartridge or tips.
Wash the column with 5 column volumes of 0.5% (vol/vol) formic acid.
Elute the bound peptides with 2 column volumes of 80% acetonitrile.
Vacuum-evaporate the eluted sample to near-dryness.
(Optional) Overlay the dried sample with 5 μl of 1 mM DTT.
(Optional) Reconstitute the dried sample in water for peptide concentration determination.
(Optional) Use an aliquot of reconstituted sample for micro BCA analysis.
Store samples at -80°C for several weeks.
Generate peak list from LC-MS/MS raw data.

Use mascot.dll plug-in for Analyst software with determination of charge state from survey scan, default precursor charge states of 2+ and 3+, MS/MS averaging of precursor scans (precursor mass tolerance for grouping = 1, maximum number of cycles between groups = 10, minimum number of cycles per group = 1).
Centroid MS/MS data.
De-isotope MS/MS data.
Reject MS/MS spectra with less than 10 peaks.
Mix peptides with the IPI database for Mascot search.
Set mass tolerance to 0.4 Da for parent ions and 0.2 Da for fragment ions in Mascot.
Allow up to two missed cleavages in Mascot searches.
Define GluC to cleave C-terminal to glutamate or both glutamate and aspartate, combining results from both searches.
Apply semi-style cleavage searches with no constraints for the orientation of specific termini.
Add static modifications: carboxyamidomethylation (+57.02 Da) on cysteine residues, dimethylation (+28.03 Da) on lysine ε-amines, and thioacylation (+88.00 Da) on amino termini.
Validate peptide identifications using PeptideProphet at a 95% confidence level.
Obtain high-confidence peptide identifications from Mascot and/or PeptideProphet for PICS analysis.
Follow instructions in the PICS EXCEL spreadsheet to complete PICS analysis.
Use the PICS Perl script for bioinformatic determination of non-prime sequences.
Compile position-specific amino acid frequencies from PICS sequence data using the EXCEL spreadsheet.
Generate heat maps with pro Fit software (QuantumSoft) using template files available online.
Align PICS sequences according to their subsites.
Use a web-based utility to display PICS cleavage sites as sequence logos.
Perform a focused analysis of substrates having a particular amino acid at a specific position in the EXCEL spreadsheet.
Compare position-specific amino acid frequencies from focused analysis with those of all substrates for characterization of subsite cooperativity.
